dct_description_sm: The use of archival structures (e.g., otoliths, scales and opercular bones) for aging in fish population study is a well-established practice in fisheries ecology. When deposited, the calcium carbonate that forms the otolith is biologically inert. This property makes otoliths useful for chronologoical reconstructions. Oxygen isotopes are used  to reconstruct organism thermal histories. Here oxygen isotopes are being used to address identified knowledge gaps with respect to Arctic char by determining [1] if there are spatial (regional) differences in thermal habitat use by Arctic char that may be coupled to differences in the observed zoogeographic patterns of growth, maturity and size-at-age and overall productivity; [2] if temporal variations in thermal habitat use by Arctic char are correlated with measured variations in regional climate (e.g., temperature); and [3] to attempt to couple variations in thermal habitat use to variations in Hg loading.
dct_title_s: Climate Variability and Change (CVC) Effects on Char in the Arctic - Oxygen Isotope Data for Juvenile Arctic Char
